author: Semo_abdu
quote: 0/10 – Grand Theft Auto has lost its identity.I waited 13 years for this game. Thirteen **** years. And what did I get? A game that feels more like Red Dead Redemption 2 than Grand Theft Auto.Rockstar seems to have forgotten what made GTA special in the first place: freedom, chaos, outrageous satire, unrestricted criminal fun and the ability to play however you **** does stealing a car have to be complicated? Why should I worry about whether a vehicle belongs to someone in my neighbourhood? Why am I being punished for killing enemies through a criminal profile system? Why should I have to incapacitate enemies instead of simply shooting them? Why does the game judge my playstyle by labelling me a professional criminal or a psychopath?And why did Rockstar take away the freedom of carrying a full arsenal? The old GTA games let you carry different types of weapons. GTA V expanded that freedom even further. Now we’re back to carrying a limited selection and having to rely on our vehicle for the rest. Why? Who asked for this downgrade?Rockstar keeps talking about realism, but apparently realism means restricting the player. The game can have aliens, Bigfoot, and red hulk and aliens? ridiculous characters and absurd situations, but when it comes to the actual gameplay, suddenly everything has to be realistic and carefully controlled. That’s not consistency. That’s selective realism.I don’t want GTA to become Red Dead Redemption. I love Rockstar’s games, but GTA and RDR are different franchises with different identities. The slower, more restrictive mechanics that worked for Arthur Morgan don’t automatically belong in a Grand Theft Auto game.I also miss the fearless satire, outrageous humour and unapologetic personality of the older GTA games. Grand Theft Auto used to feel like a franchise where nothing was off-limits. Now I worry that Rockstar has lost some of that **** Houser’s departure makes that concern even greater. He was one of the defining creative voices behind Rockstar’s storytelling and the identity of GTA. His absence is noticeable to me, and I question whether the new creative direction understands what made this franchise special.I know the game has positive aspects, and I still have things I’m looking forward to. I waited 13 years, so of course I’m going to play it. But that doesn’t mean I have to pretend I’m happy with these decisions.I wanted the next Grand Theft Auto. I wanted more freedom, more chaos, more satire and an evolution of GTA V.Instead, what I’m seeing feels like Red Dead Redemption 2 wearing a Grand Theft Auto costume.This isn’t the GTA sequel I waited 13 years for.
